title: Spatial Variation-Aware Read Disturbance Defenses: Experimental Analysis of Real DRAM Chips and Implications on Future Solutions
problem: Read disturbance in DRAM (RowHammer, RowPress) causes bitflips when memory locations are repeatedly accessed or kept active, breaking memory isolation and worsening with technology scaling. Existing defenses suffer from high performance/energy overheads, limited effectiveness, or prohibitive hardware complexity.
motivation: Read disturbance is a fundamental security vulnerability that worsens as DRAM shrinks, requiring more efficient and effective defense mechanisms.
method: The paper characterizes spatial variation in read disturbance vulnerability across 144 real DDR4 DRAM chips representing 11 die revisions, revealing large differences in susceptibility across memory locations. Svärd dynamically adapts the aggressiveness of existing read disturbance solutions based on row-level vulnerability profiles, reducing defense overhead while maintaining effectiveness.
key_novelty: Leveraging spatial variation in read disturbance vulnerability within DRAM chips to dynamically adapt defense mechanism aggressiveness and reduce overheads.
contributions: First rigorous characterization of spatial variation in read disturbance across 144 real DDR4 DRAM chips and 11 die revisions
Svärd mechanism that dynamically adapts existing read disturbance defenses based on row-level read disturbance profiles
Demonstrates worst-case vulnerable regions experience 2× more bitflips and require order of magnitude fewer accesses to induce disturbance
Achieves significant performance improvements for five state-of-the-art read disturbance solutions

metrics.speedup: Significant performance improvements on existing defenses (specific numbers not provided)
metrics.other: Reduced defense overhead; worst-case regions show 2× bitflip increase and order-of-magnitude fewer accesses needed vs. least vulnerable regions

baselines: Five state-of-the-art read disturbance defense solutions
